```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(sxchan)
```

## Overview

**sxchan** - A modern R package for channel cross-section analysis

**gbem** - Contains the "engines" for erosion: reads from sxchan channels; modifies sxchan channels.
![](https://stochagbem.github.io/gbem/logo.png)

Tasks:

- Solve GBEM issue that relies on max erosion extent to get constrained erosion.
- Refactor to not piggyback on `sf` objects.
- Make package "complete" so as to submit to CRAN.


## The Channel Object

Channel objects are just data frames (like `sf` objects). Each row is a cross section. Columns:

- Column for planimetric cross-sections (`sfc_LINESTRING`)
- Column for profile cross-sections (`xs_profile` objects)
- Ad hoc variables to your liking (e.g., d84, roughness, ...)

At least one of the plan or profile columns must be present.

| XS#| plan (sfc_LINESTRING) | profile (xs_profile) | d84 (numeric) | roughness (numeric) |
|----|-----------------------|----------------------|---------------|---------------------|
| 1  | LINESTRING(...)       | xs_profile(...)      | 45            | 0.035               |
| 2  | LINESTRING(...)       | xs_profile(...)      | 50            | 0.030               |
| 3  | LINESTRING(...)       | xs_profile(...)      | 40            | 0.040               |
| .. | ...                   | ...                  | ...           | ...                 |
| n  | LINESTRING(...)       | xs_profile(...)      | 55            | 0.025               |


## Creating Channel Objects: From Scratch

Low level constructor by assembling parts. Examples:

```
# From simple widths
channel <- xt_channel(c(10, 15, 20))

# From existing geometries
channel <- xt_channel(linestrings)

# If you also somehow have a profile object
channel <- xt_channel(linestrings, profiles)
```

## Creating Channel Objects: Generated

### Plan view first

More commonly, create plan view from banklines. Options:

```
channel <- xt_generate_plan(banks, spacing = units::set_units(10, "m"))
channel <- xt_generate_plan(banks, n = 100)
channel <- xt_generate_plan(banks, at = units::set_units(0:100, "m"))
```

Can specify manual centerline if you have it:

```
channel <- xt_generate_plan(banks, n = 100, centerline = my_centerline)
```

## Creating Channel Objects: Generated

### Then profile view

Then, sample a DEM to create profile cross-sections:

```
channel <- xt_generate_profile(
  channel, 
  dem,
  extent_multiplier = 2,  # OR, extent_distance
  sample_n = 100          # OR, sample_distance
)
```

❓ Should there be a `side = ` specification?



## Viewing

You can plot different views of the channel using base R plotting:

```
plot(channel, what = "plan")
plot(channel, what = "profile") # 🤔
plot(channel, what = "3d")
plot(channel, what = ..., extent = c("banks", "frame")) # 🤔
```

## Exporting

Similarly: export to spatial object understood by `sf` package in case you want to do something you can't do with sxchan:

```
xt_as_sf(channel, what = "plan")
xt_as_sf(channel, what = "profile") # 🤔
xt_as_sf(channel, what = "3d")
xt_as_sf(channel, what = ..., extent = c("banks", "frame")) # 🤔

## Also available:
xt_as_sfc(...)
```

## Generating from Channels

Already saw _channel_ generators: `xt_generate_plan()` and `xt_generate_profile()`.

Other things (especially useful after eroding the channel):

- `xt_generate_banks(channel, ...)` - Generate banklines from channel.
- `xt_generate_centerline(channel, ...)` - Generate centerline from channel.

Interface will allow for different methods in the future. Maybe like this:

```
xt_generate_banks(channel, method = "linear")  # 🤔
xt_generate_banks(channel, method = banks_spline(smoothness = 0.4))  # 🤔
```

## Channel Calculations

- `xt_n_sections(channel)` - Number of cross-sections
- `xt_width(channel)` - Width of each cross-section
- `xt_width_active(channel)` - Without islands / bars.
- `xt_distance_ds(channel, centerline = NULL)` - Distance along the channel
- `xt_gradient(channel, .before = 1L, .after = 1L, .complete = FALSE)` - Gradient.

## Channel Calculations: Bank Height

```
xt_height_lb(channel)         # Height of left bank
xt_height_rb(channel)         # Height of right bank
xt_height(channel, .f = min)  # Aggregate based on function .f
```

❓ Should we include cross-sectional area?

## Channel Calculations: Erosion

How much erosion volume for a given width?

```
xt_erosion_volume(channel, width = 10, side = "left")
> Vector of erosion widths for each cross-section.
```

How much erosion width for a given volume? **NEW**

```
xt_erosion_width(channel, volume = 50, side = splitter_left(0.75))
> Vector of erosion volumes for each cross-section.
```

✅ Solves the GBEM issue of needing max possible erosion to get constrained erosion.

❓ Should dredging have this level of granularity?


These allow for channel widening by either volume or width specification.

```
xt_widen(channel, width = 10)
xt_widen(channel, volume = 50)
```



## Sides

Widening specification: simple

```
xt_widen(channel, width = 10, side = "both")
xt_widen(channel, width = 10, side = "left")
xt_widen(channel, width = 10, side = "right")
```

## Sides: splitters

Widening specification: flexible specification (all these put 75% erosion on left bank).

```
xt_widen(channel, width = 10, side = splitter_left(prop = 0.75))
xt_widen(channel, width = 10, side = splitter_right(prop = 0.25))
xt_widen(channel, width = 10, side = splitter_both(prop_left = 0.75, prop_right = 0.25))
```

"Splitters" abstract away the mechanism by which erosion is allocated. Better than saying `side = 0.75`.

```
splitter_for_coldwater <- splitter_XYZ(kernel = "tricube", shape = 0.5)
xt_widen(channel, width = 10, side = splitter_for_coldwater)
```

Splitters are functions of the channel object, returning a vector of left proportions (one for each cross section).

```{r}
splitter_left()
```

**QUESTION**: Should `prop_left + prop_right = 1` always? What if bedrock is exposed on either side?



## Sides: splitters

You can make a new splitter, too:

```
splitter_vc <- new_splitter(
  fun = function(channel) {
    <your code here>
    <possibly with parameters>
  }, 
  name = "Vincenzo's Splitter", 
  params = list(alpha = 1, beta = 2)
)

xt_widen(channel, width = 10, side = "vc")
xt_widen(channel, width = 10, side = splitter_vc(beta = 1))
```
